answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a reputation bridge: each agent stakes a deposit and earns trust only through verifiable work. A shared atlas of attested identities records every agent's history, so a fresh fake starts at zero and cannot borrow reputation. Spawning thousands of fakes is like filling an ocean one cup at a time — each identity must pay the stake and do real work, so attacker cost grows linearly while one fake vote gains almost nothing. Honest agents pay once and keep standing; attackers pay for every fake.
